basis: Open Targets clinical_indication row: drugId CHEMBL4297585, diseaseId MONDO_0002412 'disorder of glycogen metabolism', maxClinicalStage UNKNOWN, clinicalReportIds [nct01461304]. NCT01461304 (study_type EXPANDED_ACCESS, no phase): "This study is also open to patients with any type of glycogen storage disease, pyruvate carboxylase deficiency, or Barth Syndrome"; inclusion criteria "Diagnosis of disorder in long chain fatty acid oxidation, glycogen storage disease, pyruvate carboxylase deficiency, or Barth Syndrome"
note: NEW TYPE: expanded-access record standing in for a trial. The only source record that reaches this disease is an Open Targets clinical_indication row whose backing 'clinical report' is a compassionate-use / EXPANDED_ACCESS protocol with no phase and no endpoint, mapped onto the broad node 'disorder of glycogen metabolism'. GSD due to muscle-and-heart glycogen synthase deficiency (GYS1, GSD 0b) falls inside that protocol's open eligibility, but no patient with this genotype is documented and there is no controlled study - hence off_label_case rather than trial. Anyone scoring maxClinicalStage mechanically would read this row as a clinical stage for the disease; it is not one. No GYS1-specific record exists anywhere: ChEMBL has 0 rows for any glycogen-synthase-deficiency term, and Open Targets has 0 rows for MONDO_0012693 and Orphanet_308520. Triheptanoin's own ChEMBL glycogen rows are other GSDs (GSD V 2.0 NCT02432768/NCT02919631, GSD VII 2.0 NCT03642860, GSD I 0.5 NCT03665636). EMA: triheptanoin holds 10 designations; the closest is EU/3/16/1710 'Treatment of McArdle's disease' (GSD V, Positive) - recorded here - the others being fatty-acid-oxidation disorders (EU/3/20/2360, EU/3/20/2302, EU/3/15/1526, EU/3/15/1525, EU/3/15/1524, EU/3/15/1508, all Positive) plus EU/3/15/1495 (GLUT1 deficiency, Withdrawn), EU/3/12/1081 and EU/3/12/1082 (Withdrawn). None is for GSD 0b. phase_other_disease=approved rests on drug_molecule.maximumClinicalStage=APPROVAL for CHEMBL4297585; both indication tables top out at phase 3 for triheptanoin, so that OT field is uncorroborated inside these sources.

basis: EMA: {Medicine name: Prohippur, Active substance: 'benzoic acid, sodium salt', Date of designation: 11/09/2002, Intended use: 'Treatment of non-ketotic hyperglycinaemia', EU designation number: EU/3/02/111, Status: Positive}

A designation is not an approval and not a trial: sodium benzoate has no ChEMBL row for any glycine-encephalopathy term (its ChEMBL rows are psychosis 2.0 and Encephalopathy 2.0 / NCT00597909, which is a hepatic-encephalopathy study, not this disease), no Open Targets row for it (urea cycle disorder PHASE_2, schizophrenia PHASE_2_3, Alzheimer PHASE_2 - hence phase_other_disease=trial), and a ClinicalTrials.gov search for benzoate in nonketotic hyperglycinemia / glycine encephalopathy returned 0 studies. off_label_case rather than not_found because unlicensed clinical use in this disease is what the designation is premised on; the clinical-practice part of that is model knowledge, not a source. Sodium benzoate holds many other designations (urea cycle disorders: EU/3/16/1705-1708, EU/3/15/1600-1601, EU/3/16/1729-1730, EU/3/16/1787-1788, EU/3/19/2166) - EU/3/02/111 is the one matching this disease.

basis: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00461799, detailed description: 'Unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia in Crigler-Najjar (CN) disease is conventionally treated with phototherapy and/or phenobarbital.'
